newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIA SEMIS-Victoria remains in spotlight.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIA SEMIS-Victoria remains in spotlight.

text.p: *Victoria remained in the spotlight last week with S&P
affirming its ratings and TCV holding a bond tender.
The Australian state of Victoria remained in the spotlight last week after Standard & Poor's affirmed its A1 plus/AA plus local currency ratings and said its outlook was stable.

"The rating fully factors in the anticipated continuation of the sound underlying budgetary position, and the support to the state's overall finances from the planned privatisation of the remaining state-owned electricity generation companies," the U.S. rating agency said.
A week earlier, Moody's Investors Service said there was scope for a further upgrading, although this was not imminent.
Treasury Corp of Victoria (TCV), the state's borrowing arm, also stepped up to the plate with a A$100 million bond tender in its November 2006 bond.

Traders said the tender went off without a hitch, fetching a weighted average yield of 7.9875 pct and with bids coming in a tight 7.985 to 7.99 bid range. The spread to Australia Treasury bonds was 20 basis points.

Semi government yields showed a tightening bias in the past week, which partly reflected swap related activity amid the re-emergence of yen/Australia dollar dual currency issues after nearly a two month break, traders said.

Australia debt yields have spiked up sharply in recent weeks on the back of signs of a pick-up in the economy and against the back drop of weak U.S. Treasuries, making the market attractive again to yield hungary Japanese investors.
Meanwhile, the state premiers conference with the Federal government is being held in Canberra on Friday.
"There maybe some movement on spreads depending on how the Commonwealth treats the states on funding," said Stephen Halmarick, Australian bond and cuurency strategist at NatWest Markets Australia.
